basis: Second review, after the edit stage. Read 1-fast.md (signals, traps, compare tables), 2-deep.md (exam signals, traps, numbers), 5-quiz.md (18 shipped questions) and data/13-route53/questions.json (status, layer, difficulty, bullets, twin_of) as an item writer, against the registry bullets of chapter 13 (2.2.K1, 2.2.K6, 2.2.S2, 3.4.S1, 4.4.K7), SPEC.json question rules and FREQUENCY.md rows 51 and 130 to 132. Shipped: 9 core and 9 extended; 3 multiple-response (q015, q013, q012); 3 twin pairs (q003/q009, q004/q014, q005/q011); difficulty 3 easy, 12 medium, 3 hard. Every bullet has a section and at least one question.

findings.quote: **Twin.** If the stem said "an operator must approve each failover" instead: change weights by hand, and accept that [this is a control plane operation](../facts/route53.md#route53-dr-weight-change-is-control-plane).
findings.evidence: The twin keeps the rest of the stem, which still requires the plan to work 'even if the Route 53 control plane is impaired' and asks for the MOST resilient steps. Changing weights fails that requirement by the chapter's own teaching. The cited source says the opposite of the twin's advice: fact route53-dr-weight-change-is-control-plane quote 'However, be aware this is a control plane operation and therefore not as resilient as the data plane approach using Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC).' So for manually approved failover AWS points to a data plane mechanism, not to weight edits. As written the twin teaches a wrong answer to a realistic exam variant. Fix: rewrite the twin so that the changed phrase also drops the impairment requirement (for example 'If the stem said "the Route 53 control plane works normally, and an operator must approve each failover"'), or name the data plane option that the quote names; do not present weight edits as the answer under impairment.
findings.resolution: fix-13: q013 twin rewritten (see claims-02): 'keep the failover records and switch them with ARC routing control; AWS recommends [features like Route 53 health checks and ARC routing control that rely on data plane functionality](route53-bp-control-plane-prioritizes-consistency-not-availability).' Weight edits are no longer presented as the answer. Twin field only; stem, options, key and explanation byte-identical, no reset.

findings.quote: Geolocation alias records: a Europe record that points to the eu-west-1 load balancer, and a Default record for the us-east-1 load balancer.
findings.evidence: FREQUENCY.md row 130 reports 'Route 53 latency vs geolocation vs geoproximity' as commonly asked, and row 51 'All routing policies'. No shipped question uses geoproximity routing as the key or as a distractor (the latency/geolocation pair q004/q014 offers geolocation, weighted and IP-based only), and 2-deep.md teaches geoproximity only in a Go deeper block. Verified facts exist: route53-choose-geoproximity-routing-resource-location-bias, route53-geoproximity-bias-expands-or-shrinks-region, route53-change-geoproximity-records-console-2024-01. Add one question whose deciding phrase is 'send more users to one Region by enlarging the area it serves' with latency and geolocation records as distractors, or at least add geoproximity as a named distractor in q004 or q014's replacement. (Repeated from the first review, exam-06.)
findings.resolution: fix-13 (deferred, not disputed): a geoproximity question is a new item that must pass the three-lens blind panel, and a new candidate now would keep the chapter from finalizing; adding geoproximity to the options of q004 or q014 would reset two verified questions. In this stage the fast file gets a sharper geoproximity signal (signals guard 'one Region must serve a larger area: geoproximity records with a bias'; compare row 'Should one Region serve a larger or smaller area?' with fact route53-geoproximity-bias-expands-or-shrinks-region). Logged for the W13/W14 question top-up.

findings.evidence: Task 4.4 is 'Design cost-optimized network architectures', but none of the four questions mapped to 4.4.K7 asks for cost (qualifiers: none / LEAST downtime / LEAST operational overhead). The chapter teaches three cost facts that decide real stems and no question tests them: route53-pricing-alias-free-for-listed-aws-services and route53-alias-queries-free-cname-charged (alias queries to AWS resources are free, CNAME queries are charged), route53-ttl-longer-cheaper-shorter-faster-change ('A longer TTL reduces your Route 53 charges'). Add one MOST cost-effective question (for example alias vs CNAME for a subdomain on a load balancer at high query volume) or rewrite the qualifier of q001's replacement.
findings.resolution: fix-13 (deferred, not disputed): the chapter's MOST cost-effective item (q002) was rejected by the blind panel, and a replacement is a new candidate that must pass the panel; changing the qualifier of a verified question resets it. Logged for the W13/W14 question top-up (alias vs CNAME query charges, longer TTL).

findings.quote: Users in South America, and some users whose location cannot be identified, get no answer from DNS. These users must be served from us-east-1.
findings.evidence: The stem says 'serves users around the world' and has records only for Europe and North America, so users in Asia, Africa and Oceania also get no answer, but the requirement names only South America and unmapped users. The key (one Default record) also sends Asia, Africa and Oceania to us-east-1, which the stem does not ask for, in a scenario framed by 'distribution rights' (fact route53-geolocation-use-cases: content for 'only the locations where you have distribution rights'). A careful reader can argue that the 'each remaining continent' option is safer. Make the requirement cover everyone: 'All users outside Europe and North America, and users whose location cannot be identified, must be served from us-east-1.' This changes the stem, so the item goes back through the blind panel.
findings.resolution: fix-13: q007 no longer ships (exam-05), so the stem does not reach the reader. Note for a later edit: the gap cannot move the key, because both options that serve the remaining users (c and d) also send the other continents to us-east-1, and d does it with one record; the panel was unanimous. The stem stays unchanged in the verified pool.

findings.section: Signals and traps; Choose it or not / Routing by latency or by location
findings.quote: | "a specific country", "distribution rights" | geolocation records and a default record | content for [only the locations where you have distribution rights] | traffic shifts step by step between Regions: geoproximity records |
findings.evidence: 'Traffic shifts step by step' is the signal of weighted records (the next row: 'a small share of users on a new version'), not of geoproximity. Geoproximity routes by the location of resources and a bias that 'expands or shrinks the geographic region from which traffic goes to a resource' (fact route53-geoproximity-bias-expands-or-shrinks-region). A stem with 'shift traffic gradually to the new Region' then points her to the wrong policy. The compare table row 'Should traffic move from one place to another? | Geoproximity' has the same vagueness. Use the bias phrase in both places: 'one Region must serve a larger area than its neighbour: geoproximity records with a bias'.
findings.resolution: fix-13: signals guard now 'one Region must serve a larger area: geoproximity records with a bias'; compare row now 'Should one Region serve a larger or smaller area? | Geoproximity | By resource location. [A bias expands or shrinks the geographic region](route53-geoproximity-bias-expands-or-shrinks-region)'; the deciding question says 'an area to grow or shrink around a Region'.

findings.quote: | "zone apex", "root domain" | an alias record | ... | the target is a name outside AWS: a CNAME record, on a subdomain |
findings.evidence: STYLE.md 11.9: a 'but not if' guard names the case where the same stem phrase leads elsewhere. A stem that says 'zone apex' cannot move to a subdomain, so 'a CNAME record, on a subdomain' never answers it. For an apex whose target is outside AWS an alias record does not work (fact route53-alias-targets-only-selected-aws-resources: 'An alias record can only redirect queries to selected AWS resources') and a CNAME record is not allowed (route53-cname-dns-protocol-forbids-zone-apex); the record that works there is an A record with the address. Write the guard for that case, and keep the subdomain CNAME case in the compare table. (Partly fixed since the first review, exam-02.)
findings.resolution: fix-13: the guard now names the apex case: 'the target is outside AWS: an A record with its IP address'. The subdomain CNAME case stays in the compare table and the 2-deep Stop and answer.

findings.quote: Users must move to the new site with minimal downtime, and the team must be able to roll back quickly if the new site fails. Which approach will meet these requirements with the LEAST downtime for users?
findings.evidence: The stem does not say that the data center servers stop on Saturday. If they keep running, the 'change on Saturday' option causes no downtime (cached users still reach working old servers), so 'LEAST downtime' does not separate it from the key; what separates them is how fast all users move and how fast a roll back reaches them. The stem also states the goal twice ('minimal downtime' and 'LEAST downtime'). Add 'The data center servers will be shut down on Saturday evening.' or change the qualifier to the speed of the move and the roll back. (Repeated from the first review, exam-08; the stem is unchanged.)
findings.resolution: fix-13: the gap cannot change the key, so a stem edit (which resets the verified question) is not justified. The stem requires that users 'move to the new site'. Under option a, cached users stay on the old site for up to the old TTL whether or not the old servers keep running, so a never moves users faster than b; if the old servers stop, a also causes downtime. b is the best answer under both readings, and the three solvers agreed. Kept as a note for a later stem polish.

findings.quote: Route 53 keeps policies apart: [you can't create non-latency records](../facts/route53.md#route53-latency-no-non-latency-record-same-name-type) with the name and type of latency records, so the two kinds cannot share a name.
findings.evidence: The option adds a latency record next to existing geolocation records; the cited fact covers the other direction (creating non-latency records next to latency records). The conclusion follows only by inference. Prefer a fact that names the general rule, or explain with the chapter's own Go deeper fact: to combine policies for one name, AWS uses alias records in a decision tree (route53-complex-config-latency-alias-weighted-tree).
findings.resolution: fix-13: fixed with claims-08: q007 option b why now explains with route53-complex-config-latency-alias-weighted-tree (alias records in a decision tree). q007 also no longer ships.

findings.quote: Latency alias records for the two load balancers, one record for each Region, with Evaluate Target Health set to Yes on both records.
findings.evidence: q020's key is nearly the same option as q004's key ('Latency alias records for the two load balancers, one record in each Region, with Evaluate Target Health turned on for both records'), so a reader who remembers q004 answers q020 by recall. q020 tests active-active latency versus failover; that concept is worth keeping, but give it a different surface (for example Network Load Balancers or a primary in one Region plus latency in two) or swap it for the verified q022.
findings.resolution: fix-13: q020 and q004 test different deciding phrases (active-active versus failover; latency versus location). The shared key text is the correct configuration in both, and the distractors differ. A new surface means new options, which resets a verified difficulty 3 question; after the reorder the two items are 12 positions apart (Questions 4 and 16).

findings.section: Weighted records give each resource its share of the total weight
findings.evidence: Multivalue answer routing is examinable (q010 is about it; 1-fast signals row 'several healthy IP addresses, no load balancer') but it has no heading of its own: it lives in one table row and one Exam trap inside the weighted subsection, and q010's Review link points to 'Weighted records give each resource its share of the total weight'. From the skim of headings she cannot find it. Mention multivalue answer records in the subsection heading or give the table a caption that names both policies.
findings.resolution: fix-13: the H3 heading texts are fixed by brief.json (R4; L905 checks them), and 2-deep.md is at 4496 of its 4500 words, so a caption sentence does not fit. The 1-fast signals row names multivalue answer records. Logged for the orchestrator as a brief heading change.

findings.quote: Create a Lambda function that rewrites A and AAAA records for example.com with the distribution's addresses every minute.
findings.evidence: Item-writer view: in a 'Select TWO' item with a LEAST operational overhead qualifier, a scheduled Lambda that rewrites records is an option nobody picks, so the item has effectively four options. A distractor built on a real misconception would teach more, for example 'Create an alias record of type A only; CloudFront answers IPv6 clients through it' (contradicted by route53-alias-cloudfront-ipv6-two-records).
findings.resolution: fix-13: replacing an option changes what the blind panel saw and resets a verified question; this is a note-level item-writing preference. Logged for a later revision.
